title: 1974: his Italian teacher slaps him into playing
summary: At sixteen or seventeen Howard refused to play a solo at Altamont Park, so his teacher slapped him; he played Victor Herbert and stopped the show.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Triple-tonguing and double-tonguing (Demonstrating). I could do all of them, play those solos. And most all of those things. So one day in Atamont Park. I'm trying to think what city it was.

Yeah, it was a city in Ohio somewhere. I'll have to think, someplace. Anyhow, I wouldn't go out and play, and my teacher used to go with me. He was an Italian fellow. He used to go with me everywhere I went. And I wouldn't
go out and play, but you know what he did? He hit me in the jaw.
Yeah. Hit me in the jaw. Took his open hand and slapped the devil out of me.

Because I wouldn't play. Said, "You're going to go out there and play." I looked out there and seen all them people and got scared to death. I wouldn't go. He said, "You're going to go play." Now, I'm still around 16, 17 years old, just a kid. Wham. So I knew I had to do it or else my father would have took charge of me when I got home, so I went on and played, and got a big hand and everything, stopped the show, as they call it. I don't know what it was. But I'm trying to think of some of the tunes that I played. "Rider of the Waves," is one of them, by Victor Herbert. And, oh, there's some more. Just different tunes that people knew. They didn't know all -- they didn't have no ragtime or nothing then.
